## 1. History

### Early Origins (1960s-1970s)

| Year | Contribution |
|------|-------------|
| 1960s | **Henry J. Kelley** and **Arthur Bryson** developed precursor ideas in optimal control theory |
| 1970 | **Seppo Linnainmaa** (Finnish) formalized the **reverse mode automatic differentiation** - the true mathematical foundation |
| 1974 | **Paul Werbos** proposed backpropagation for neural networks in his PhD thesis (largely ignored) |

### The Breakthrough (1986)

In 1986, **David Rumelhart**, **Geoffrey Hinton**, and **Ronald Williams** published the seminal paper:

> *"Learning representations by back-propagating errors"*
> Nature, 323(6088), 533-536

This paper:
- Popularized the algorithm for training multilayer networks
- Showed that hidden layers learn useful internal representations
- Sparked renewed interest in neural networks

### Deep Learning Revolution (2012-Present)

| Year | Event |
|------|-------|
| 1989 | **Yann LeCun** applied backprop to handwriting recognition (ZIP codes) |
| 2006 | **Geoffrey Hinton** demonstrated deep belief networks (pre-training) |
| 2012 | **AlexNet** (Krizhevsky et al.) won ImageNet using backprop + GPUs |
| 2012+ | Backprop enabled the deep learning revolution across all domains |

---

## 2. The Forward Pass

### Network Architecture

Consider a simple feedforward network:

```
Input (x) → Linear → Activation → Linear → Output (ŷ)
            W₁, b₁                   W₂, b₂
```

For a single sample with batch size = 1:

```
z₁ = x · W₁ᵀ + b₁      (linear transformation)
a₁ = σ(z₁)              (activation function)
z₂ = a₁ · W₂ᵀ + b₂     (output linear transformation)
ŷ = softmax(z₂)         (output activation, e.g., for classification)
```

### Notation Conventions

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Symbol          │  Meaning                                      │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  x ∈ ℝ^(1×n)     │  Input vector (1 sample, n features)         │
│  W₁ ∈ ℝ^(n×h)    │  Weights layer 1 (n inputs → h hidden)       │
│  b₁ ∈ ℝ^(1×h)    │  Bias layer 1                                │
│  z₁ ∈ ℝ^(1×h)    │  Pre-activation layer 1                      │
│  a₁ ∈ ℝ^(1×h)    │  Post-activation layer 1                     │
│  W₂ ∈ ℝ^(h×c)    │  Weights layer 2 (h hidden → c classes)      │
│  b₂ ∈ ℝ^(1×c)    │  Bias layer 2                                │
│  z₂ ∈ ℝ^(1×c)
